*Officials advise no swimming, recreational ocean activities on north- and west-facing shores*

HANALEI *– *Ocean Safety Bureau officials are advising no swimming or other recreational ocean activities along all north- and west-facing shores of Kauaʻi today through Thursday, Nov. 12, due to high surf and dangerous ocean conditions.

The National Weather Service has issued a High Surf Advisory for north- and west-facing shores of Kauaʻi and Niʻihau, in effect until 6 p.m. Thursday.

According to the NWS, a large north-northwest swell will build through the day, with surf rising to 15 to 20 feet along north-facing shores and 10 to 15 feet along west-facing shores. Surf is expected to peak tonight at 18 to 24 feet on north-facing shores and 14 to 18 feet on west-facing shores, possibly into Thursday morning, before dropping below advisory levels Thursday night.

Forecasters also expect breezy trade winds, with strong, gusty winds possible on Kauaʻi. A Small Craft Advisory is in effect for Kauaʻi waters until 6 a.m. Thursday. Another swell this weekend could bring surf back to advisory levels.

As a safety precaution, OSB officials have posted warning signs and are monitoring the area.

Entering the water in these areas in hazardous ocean conditions could cause serious injury or death. Beachgoers are also advised to use extreme caution, as large breaking waves could make it dangerous for those standing along the shoreline. When in doubt, don’t go out.

Beachgoers are urged to heed all posted warnings and advisories.

For updated information on ocean and weather alerts, visit the NWS website, www.weather.gov/hfo.

For up-to-date information about Kauaʻi ocean conditions and ocean safety, please speak to a county lifeguard at any lifeguard station, visit safebeachday.com/county/kauai, or call the Ocean Safety Bureau at 808-241-4984. View as web page

*Temporary green waste sites in Kapaʻa and Kīlauea to close Nov. 17*

LĪHUʻE – The County of Kauaʻi Department of Public Works Solid Waste Division will close its temporary green waste sites in Kapaʻa and Kīlauea on Tuesday, Nov. 17.

The two sites opened after Hurricane Lowell as a short-term option to help residents clear storm-related green waste. Closing them on schedule keeps the County’s storm debris operations within federal disaster recovery requirements.

“These sites were set up to help our ʻohana clean up after the storm, and they were always meant to be temporary,” said Mayor Derek S.K. Kawakami. “Closing them now is the responsible step to protect the recovery funding our island depends on. Mahalo to our Solid Waste team for keeping these sites running, and to everyone who came out with patience and aloha.”

After Nov. 17, residents may continue to recycle green waste at the following County facilities, open daily except holidays:


* Hanalei Refuse Transfer Station, 5-3751 Kūhiō Highway, Princeville. Green waste is accepted from 8 a.m. to 3 p.m.
* Kapaʻa Refuse Transfer Station, 5051 Kahi Road, Kapaʻa. 7:15 a.m. to 3:15 p.m.
* Līhuʻe Refuse Transfer Station, 3450 Ahukini Road, Līhuʻe. 7:15 a.m. to 3:15 p.m.
* Hanapēpē Refuse Transfer Station, 4380 Lele Road, Hanapēpē. 7:15 a.m. to 3:15 p.m.
* Kekaha Landfill, 6900-D Kaumualiʻi Highway, Kekaha. 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., closed for lunch from noon to 12:30 p.m.

Green waste is also accepted for a fee at these permitted private facilities. Please call ahead for hours and rates:


* Heart and Soul Organics, 6020 Koʻolau Road, Moloaʻa. 808-823-1007
* Green Earth Matters, next to Heart and Soul Organics, Moloaʻa. 808-651-2058
* Kauai Nursery and Landscaping, 3-1550 Kaumualiʻi Highway, Līhuʻe. 808-245-7747

Green waste includes lawn trimmings, yard waste, tree trimmings, stumps, branches, leaves, and shrubbery. Only green waste is accepted. Remove all rope, tarps, plastic bags, and tie-downs before dropping off. Logs and stumps 8 inches or more in diameter should be cut to 8 feet or less.

Through Nov. 17, there is no fee to drop off Hurricane Lowell debris at County refuse transfer stations or the Kekaha Landfill. The fee waiver, part of the County emergency order signed Sept. 18, applies to homes and businesses and covers hurricane debris only.

*Nov. 9, Hurricane Lowell recovery, County of Kauaʻi services update*

*LĪHUʻE – *Please see the latest updates on Hurricane Lowell recovery and County of Kauaʻi services below.

*Hurricane Lowell Recovery*

*_Hurricane Lowell CASPER survey next week_*

The Hawaiʻi Department of Health’s Kauaʻi District Health Office and the County of Kauaʻi will conduct a Community Assessment for Public Health Emergency Response (CASPER) survey Nov. 16 to 20 to learn about Hurricane Lowell impacts and ongoing recovery needs. The results will help guide recovery work by county, state, and federal partners and community organizations.


* Teams will go door to door in 30 randomly selected areas, visiting seven homes in each area.
* Teams are made up of DOH staff, supported by the Kauaʻi Medical Reserve Corps and KEMA. Members will wear identifying vests and carry ID cards.
* The survey takes less than 10 minutes and is voluntary. Responses are confidential, and no names or addresses are collected. Households may also complete the survey by phone.
* Questions cover emergency supplies right after the storm, physical and economic impacts, health and well-being, and recovery needs.
* Results will be shared in a public report. Past Kauaʻi CASPER reports are at https://health.hawaii.gov/kauai/Casper.

*_Relief grants for farmers and ranchers_*

Farmers and ranchers whose agricultural lands were affected by Hurricane Lowell and other recent storms may apply for up to $1,500 through the state’s Emergency Farmer Relief grant program. Applications close Jan. 29, 2027.


* Farms, orchards, ranches, and similar operations statewide are eligible. Limit one $1,500 check per applicant per year.
* Applicants must provide tax documents such as a W-9, Schedule C, or Schedule F.
* Funding is limited. If applications exceed available funds, they will be processed first-come, first-served.
* Checks are expected to be available for pickup statewide starting early to mid-January. Applicants will be notified of the time and place.

* Apply at https://dab.hawaii.gov. For questions, email dab.info@hawaii.gov or call (808) 973-9560.

*_Business Recovery Grants_*

Due to high demand, the Kauaʻi Hurricane Lowell Business Recovery Grant Program is no longer accepting applications. Businesses and nonprofits can join the waitlist at https://kauaibusinessrecovery.org in case more funding becomes available.

2026-11-05T22:51:22 [water]
*Housing Agency acquires 155 acres in Līhu‘e for future
affordable housing development*

LĪHU‘E – The Housing Agency announces the acquisition of 155 acres of vacant land in Līhuʻe for future affordable housing development, marking another significant step toward expanding housing opportunities for Kauaʻi residents.

Purchased from Grove Farm Properties, Inc. for $3.7 million, the property is expected to accommodate approximately 400 to 500 new homes, based on preliminary assessments of the site's buildable land. Once developed, the project will become the County’s fourth master-planned affordable housing subdivision, adding to ongoing efforts to create permanently affordable homeownership opportunities for Kauaʻi’s working families.

“Every opportunity to create more housing brings us one step closer to helping local families put down roots and build their future here on Kaua‘i. We’re grateful to Grove Farm for being such a great partner and for working with us to make this opportunity possible,” said Mayor Derek S.K. Kawakami. “While this property has the potential to provide hundreds of new homes, it’s important that we take the time to plan thoughtfully and listen to the community as we shape what comes next. Our goal is to create a neighborhood that serves our residents for generations to come.”

While the estimated number of homes provides an initial picture of the property's potential, the County will undertake a community-based master planning process to help shape the future development. This process will allow KCHA to take a closer look at the site’s opportunities and constraints, while gathering community input to help determine the number and types of homes, as well as the amenities and other features that may be incorporated into the subdivision.

The master planning process will help establish a more detailed vision for the property and guide future development decisions. The timeline for the planning process and subsequent development has not yet been determined.

The County of Kaua‘i remains committed to pursuing long-term solutions to Kauaʻi’s housing needs by creating more opportunities for local families to find and maintain a place to call home.

Additional information, including announcements about upcoming community meetings, will be shared as it becomes available.

For updates on this project and other County affordable housing initiatives, visit www.kauai.gov/housing . View as web page

GD-PIO NR 11-03-26 (Swimmer rescued from waters off Secret Beach Monday)
2026-11-04T01:00:59 [weather]
*Swimmer rescued from waters off Secret Beach Monday*

LĪHU‘E  — Personnel from the Kaua‘i Fire Department rescued a 21-year-old male visitor from the waters off Secret Beach on Monday, November 2, after he was found in distress approximately 70 yards offshore.

Personnel with the Hanalei Fire Station responded and accessed the beach via the trail off Kalihiwai Road. Upon arrival, firefighters located the swimmer near the north side of the beach in a large rip current, with surf conditions reaching an estimated 10 to 15 feet.

Two firefighters entered the water, reached the swimmer within minutes, and secured him with a rescue tube. An Ocean Safety Bureau North Shore roving rescue jet ski also responded and assisted in securing the swimmer and rescuers beyond the breaking waves. Due to the large surf conditions, Rescue 3 aboard Air 1 responded to the incident shortly before 11:28 a.m. to assist with extraction. Air 1 safely transported the swimmer to shore using a Billy Pugh rescue net.

The swimmer was transferred to awaiting American Medical Response personnel and transported to Wilcox Medical Center for further treatment. The two firefighters involved in the water rescue were also safely extracted by Air 1.

The scene was cleared shortly after 12:20 p.m. View as web page

*Nov. 9, Hurricane Lowell recovery, County of Kauaʻi services update*

*LĪHUʻE – *Please see the latest updates on Hurricane Lowell recovery and County of Kauaʻi services below.

*Hurricane Lowell Recovery*

*_Hurricane Lowell CASPER survey next week_*

The Hawaiʻi Department of Health’s Kauaʻi District Health Office and the County of Kauaʻi will conduct a Community Assessment for Public Health Emergency Response (CASPER) survey Nov. 16 to 20 to learn about Hurricane Lowell impacts and ongoing recovery needs. The results will help guide recovery work by county, state, and federal partners and community organizations.


  * Teams will go door to door in 30 randomly selected areas, visiting seven homes in each area. 
  * Teams are made up of DOH staff, supported by the Kauaʻi Medical Reserve Corps and KEMA. Members will wear identifying vests and carry ID cards. 
  * The survey takes less than 10 minutes and is voluntary. Responses are confidential, and no names or addresses are collected. Households may also complete the survey by phone. 
  * Questions cover emergency supplies right after the storm, physical and economic impacts, health and well-being, and recovery needs. 
  * Results will be shared in a public report. Past Kauaʻi CASPER reports are at https://health.hawaii.gov/kauai/Casper. 

*_Relief grants for farmers and ranchers_*

Farmers and ranchers whose agricultural lands were affected by Hurricane Lowell and other recent storms may apply for up to $1,500 through the state’s Emergency Farmer Relief grant program. Applications close Jan. 29, 2027.


  * Farms, orchards, ranches, and similar operations statewide are eligible. Limit one $1,500 check per applicant per year. 
  * Applicants must provide tax documents such as a W-9, Schedule C, or Schedule F. 
  * Funding is limited. If applications exceed available funds, they will be processed first-come, first-served. 
  * Checks are expected to be available for pickup statewide starting early to mid-January. Applicants will be notified of the time and place. 

  * Apply at https://dab.hawaii.gov. For questions, email dab.info@hawaii.gov or call (808) 973-9560. 

*_Business Recovery Grants_*

Due to high demand, the Kauaʻi Hurricane Lowell Business Recovery Grant Program is no longer accepting applications. Businesses and nonprofits can join the waitlist at https://kauaibusinessrecovery.org in case more funding becomes available.

*_Help for nonprofits_*

The U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) is offering low-interest disaster loans of up to $2 million to eligible private nonprofit and faith-based organizations affected by Hurricane Lowell.


  * Deadlines are Dec. 7 for physical damage and July 7, 2027, for economic injury. 
  * Apply at https://www.sba.gov/disaster or call (866) 722-4357.

REMINDER: EISPN Notice and Waiahi Surface Water Treatment Plant public scoping meeting Nov. 10 & 12

LĪHUʻE - The Kaua‘i Department of Water (KDOW) is publishing the Environmental Impact Statement Preparation Notice (EISPN) for the acquisition and expansion of the Waiahi Surface Water Treatment Plant and Upgrade of the Related Waterline Transmission System (“Project”) for public review. The *EISPN document will be available to download* from the* State of Hawaii - Environmental Review Program website on November 8, 2026:*

headline.title: Housing Agency acquires 155 acres in Līhu‘e for future affordable housing development
headline.subject: NR 11-05-26 (Housing Agency acquires 155 acres in Līhu‘e for future affordable housing development)

items.body:
*Housing Agency acquires 155 acres in Līhu‘e for future
affordable housing development*

LĪHU‘E – The Housing Agency announces the acquisition of 155 acres of vacant land in Līhuʻe for future affordable housing development, marking another significant step toward expanding housing opportunities for Kauaʻi residents.

Purchased from Grove Farm Properties, Inc. for $3.7 million, the property is expected to accommodate approximately 400 to 500 new homes, based on preliminary assessments of the site's buildable land. Once developed, the project will become the County’s fourth master-planned affordable housing subdivision, adding to ongoing efforts to create permanently affordable homeownership opportunities for Kauaʻi’s working families.

“Every opportunity to create more housing brings us one step closer to helping local families put down roots and build their future here on Kaua‘i. We’re grateful to Grove Farm for being such a great partner and for working with us to make this opportunity possible,” said Mayor Derek S.K. Kawakami. “While this property has the potential to provide hundreds of new homes, it’s important that we take the time to plan thoughtfully and listen to the community as we shape what comes next. Our goal is to create a neighborhood that serves our residents for generations to come.”

While the estimated number of homes provides an initial picture of the property's potential, the County will undertake a community-based master planning process to help shape the future development. This process will allow KCHA to take a closer look at the site’s opportunities and constraints, while gathering community input to help determine the number and types of homes, as well as the amenities and other features that may be incorporated into the subdivision.

The master planning process will help establish a more detailed vision for the property and guide future development decisions. The timeline for the planning process and subsequent development has not yet been determined.

The County of Kaua‘i remains committed to pursuing long-term solutions to Kauaʻi’s housing needs by creating more opportunities for local families to find and maintain a place to call home.

Additional information, including announcements about upcoming community meetings, will be shared as it becomes available.

For updates on this project and other County affordable housing initiatives, visit www.kauai.gov/housing .

LĪHUʻE – In observance of the Veterans Day holiday, County of Kauaʻi offices and all neighborhood centers will be closed on Wednesday, Nov. 11.

Closures also include the following facilities:


  * 

All refuse transfer stations;


  * 

The Kekaha Landfill;


  * 

All HI5 Redemption Centers;


  * 

The Līhuʻe Redemption Center;


  * 

The Puhi Metals Recycling Facility; and


  * 

The Kapaʻa swimming pool.

The Kauaʻi Bus will be operating on its current daily schedule. 

Regular business hours for county offices and services will resume on Thursday, Nov. 12.

For more information on recreation services, please visit the Department of Parks and Recreation website, www.kauai.gov/Parks , or call 808-241-4460.

For more information about The Kauaʻi Bus, please visit the Transportation website, www.kauai.gov/transportation , or call 808-246-8110.

For more information about recycling and waste disposal, please visit the Recycling website, www.kauai.gov/recycling , or call 808-241-4841. Please see www.kauai.gov/HI5  for location information for HI5 recycling.

headline.subject: DOW NR 11-04-2026 (EISPN Notice and Waiahi Surface Water Treatment Plant public scoping meeting on Nov. 10 & 12)

items.body:
EISPN Notice and Waiahi Surface Water Treatment Plant public scoping meeting on Nov. 10 & 12

LĪHUʻE - The Kaua‘i Department of Water (KDOW) is publishing the Environmental Impact Statement Preparation Notice (EISPN) for the acquisition and expansion of the Waiahi Surface Water Treatment Plant and Upgrade of the Related Waterline Transmission System (“Project”) for public review. The *EISPN document will be available to download* from the* State of Hawaii - Environmental Review Program website on November 8, 2026:*

Website: https://planning.hawaii.gov/erp/environmental-notice/ 

Direct link to EISPN (accessible on November 8): https://files.hawaii.gov/dbedt/erp/Doc_Library/2026-11-08-KA-EISPN-Waiahi-Surface-Water-Treatment-Plant-and-Transmission-System.pdf 

The EISPN publication and public review period provides an opportunity for agencies and the public to provide input on the environmental, social, and technical issues that should be evaluated as part of the draft Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) being prepared. The 30-day public review period is from November 8 to December 8, 2026. *The deadline for submitting comments is December 8, 2026. *

KDOW invites the public to attend the EISPN scoping meetings to learn more about the Project and share their feedback. Two EISPN scoping meetings will be held during the 30-day public review period: *              *

*MEETING INFORMATION*

*EISPN Scoping Meeting (Virtual) *

*Date/Time:* November 10, 2026, at 5 p.m.
*Access Link: *    https://us06web.zoom.us/j/81073415164  
Passcode: 613829

*EISPN Scoping Meeting (In-person) – All-day open house with three scheduled presentations*

*Date/Start Time*: November 12, 2026, at 10 a.m.
*Presentations: *12 p.m., 4:30 p.m., 6:30 p.m.
*Location: *Kaua‘i War Memorial Convention Hall, 4191 Hardy Street, Līhu‘e

To learn more about the Project or to submit general or EISPN comments, visit https://waiahi-swtp-eis.com/ .

For more information on meeting locations, email publicrelations@kauaiwater.org or call 808-245-5455.

items.from: County of Kaua'i Public Information Officer <CountyofKauaiPIO@public.govdelivery.com>
items.subject: NR 11-03-26 (Swimmer rescued from waters off Secret Beach Monday)

headline.title: Swimmer rescued from waters off Secret Beach Monday
headline.subject: NR 11-03-26 (Swimmer rescued from waters off Secret Beach Monday)

items.body:
*Swimmer rescued from waters off Secret Beach Monday*

LĪHU‘E  — Personnel from the Kaua‘i Fire Department rescued a 21-year-old male visitor from the waters off Secret Beach on Monday, November 2, after he was found in distress approximately 70 yards offshore.

Personnel with the Hanalei Fire Station responded and accessed the beach via the trail off Kalihiwai Road. Upon arrival, firefighters located the swimmer near the north side of the beach in a large rip current, with surf conditions reaching an estimated 10 to 15 feet.

Two firefighters entered the water, reached the swimmer within minutes, and secured him with a rescue tube. An Ocean Safety Bureau North Shore roving rescue jet ski also responded and assisted in securing the swimmer and rescuers beyond the breaking waves. Due to the large surf conditions, Rescue 3 aboard Air 1 responded to the incident shortly before 11:28 a.m. to assist with extraction. Air 1 safely transported the swimmer to shore using a Billy Pugh rescue net.

The swimmer was transferred to awaiting American Medical Response personnel and transported to Wilcox Medical Center for further treatment. The two firefighters involved in the water rescue were also safely extracted by Air 1.

The scene was cleared shortly after 12:20 p.m.
